title: Input control and outcome presentation registry
note: The compilation rules that turn a resolved schema shape plus declared ownership into a semantic control. An entry declares the shapes it accepts, the UX properties it requires, its parser and its binding. New controls become registered entries; they are never arbitrary JavaScript or HTML embedded in a capability profile. A shape with no entry stays explicitly unsupported until one is established.

policy.note: Carried from the Lab's compiled pilot defaults so the workbench does not quietly relax them.

inputControls.note: Whitespace and Unicode are preserved exactly as supplied; the declaration may not ask for normalisation the contract does not state.
Selected only when the UX declaration states the content is multiline. Shape alone never implies it.
An optional boolean that was never touched is absent, not false.
The user selects which retained example runs. The payload itself stays server-owned and is never sent by the browser.

unsupportedInputShapes.reason: A nested editable object needs a declared field group whose children bind to their own pointers. Only server-derived objects assembled from declared children are supported.
unsupportedInputShapes.wouldRequire: A group control with per-child binding and object assembly.

unsupportedInputShapes.reason: A repeating group needs stable item identities, per-item validation and contract cardinality.
unsupportedInputShapes.wouldRequire: A collection editor component and its item-identity protocol.

unsupportedInputShapes.reason: A variant selector must retain per-variant draft values separately and submit only the chosen admissible shape.
unsupportedInputShapes.wouldRequire: A variant selector control and per-variant draft state.

unsupportedInputShapes.shape: date-time, money, file and other composite values
unsupportedInputShapes.reason: A string or object shape alone does not establish the meaning. These need a registered semantic component with a parser and binding protocol.
unsupportedInputShapes.wouldRequire: A registered composite component per value kind.

outcomeFamilies.note: Returned text is escaped. Markup in an outcome is content, never markup.
A scalar whose value is the point. Currency or unit must be declared, not inferred from the number.
Domain disposition. Provider success and business success are separate facts and are never merged.
Grouped read-only fields in declared order. Missing, null and zero remain distinct.
Repeated records with a declared item path and empty-state text.
Findings carried by the outcome, with their codes and identities.
Digests, timestamps and authorised evidence references for this run.

unsupportedOutcomeFamilies.reason: A chart needs explicit series, axis, unit and missing-data mappings. An array being present is not a reason to draw one.
unsupportedOutcomeFamilies.wouldRequire: A registered chart component with declared series bindings.

unsupportedOutcomeFamilies.reason: An artifact or media result needs typed, authorised resource references and an availability state.
unsupportedOutcomeFamilies.wouldRequire: A registered artifact component and an authorised resource protocol.

deliveryStates.meaning: The service accepted the request and issued a run identity.
The service refused the request. The draft is preserved and the refusal is shown.
Delivery could not be established. A recoverable pending view is retained and the request is reconciled, never automatically resubmitted.
A validated outcome arrived and matched a declared variant.
A returned shape validated against no declared variant. A contract finding is shown with authorised diagnostic detail, never a plausible-looking success card.
